h1: The 6 Best Under-Desk Filing Cabinets of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Under-Desk File Cabinets: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six under-desk filing cabinets compared on drawers, locks, rolling bases, materials and fit for small home offices.
summary: The Letaya 3 drawer mobile cabinet is our best overall pick for a lockable, fully assembled pedestal. The SISESOL is the budget choice with a narrow profile, and the SteeLoong keeps things plain and compact. The GYIIYUO suits L-shaped desks, and the DEVAISE doubles as a printer stand.
intro: Most people measure the desk width and forget the clearance under the modesty panel, the drawer pull, and the knee space. A cabinet that technically fits can still block your legs or refuse to open fully. That is how a cheap pedestal turns into a doorstop.

We reviewed eight listings and kept six that clearly suit under-desk use, setting aside a lateral cabinet that needs more width. Ranking is based on drawer count, locks, material, mobility, assembly state and price bucket, using the spec sheets and owner feedback. None of it is bench measured.

products.name: Letaya 3 Drawer Mobile File Cabinet with Lock, Under Desk Metal Filing Cabinet, Fully Assembled
products.verdict: A lockable metal pedestal that arrives built.
products.description:
This is a three drawer metal pedestal with a lock, sold fully assembled and sized for under-desk use. It handles letter, legal and A4 documents, which is wider coverage than most compact rivals.

It ranks first because the third drawer adds capacity without raising the footprint, and the lack of assembly removes the biggest hassle. It sits in the $50-100 bucket, the same as several two drawer models.

It is right for anyone with real paperwork to store. The caveat is that three drawers use more height, so check your desk clearance first.
products.idealFor: Home offices with a real paper archive.
products.skipIf: Your desk has very low clearance.

products.name: SISESOL 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Narrow Vertical Filing Cabinet, Under Desk File Cabinet
products.verdict: The cheapest lockable metal cabinet with a narrow fit.
products.description:
The SISESOL is a narrow, vertical two drawer metal cabinet with a lock, designed for under-desk space. It takes letter, A4 and legal files and goes together with simple assembly.

It ranks second because it costs the least of the metal group, in the $25-50 bucket, while keeping a lock and a slim profile. It gives up the third drawer of the Letaya and has no wheels listed.

A good fit for small desks and dorm offices. The caveat is that it is stationary, so moving it means lifting.
products.skipIf: You want to roll it out to reach files.

products.name: SteeLoong 2 Drawer File Cabinets, Metal Office File Cabinet with Lock, Black
products.verdict: No extras, just a compact black metal pedestal.
products.description:
The SteeLoong is a two drawer metal cabinet with a lock, in black, with a compact pedestal footprint. It suits standard file sizes.

It ranks below the SISESOL on price, since it falls in the $50-100 bucket without a clearly narrower body. What you get is a plain, tidy look that blends into an office.

It fits buyers who want a no-fuss cabinet. The caveat is that the listing offers little beyond the basics.
products.skipIf: You want wheels or a work surface.

products.name: GYIIYUO 2 Drawer File Cabinet with 24 Inch Extended Desktop, Mobile Filing Cabinet with Side Bag
products.verdict: A rolling cabinet that adds a 24 inch extended top.
products.description:
This two drawer cabinet rolls on casters and carries a 24 inch extended top plus a side storage bag. The fabric drawer fronts take letter and A4 documents.

It ranks fourth because the fabric construction is lighter than the steel picks, and it has no lock listed. The payoff is mobility and extra surface for an L-shaped setup.

Buy it if you want a movable return. The caveat is that fabric drawers sag under heavy files.

products.name: DEVAISE Mobile File Cabinet, Rolling Printer Stand with Open Storage Shelf, Fabric Vertical Filing Cabinet
products.verdict: Filing drawer and printer perch in one rolling unit.
products.description:
The DEVAISE pairs a rolling file drawer with an open top shelf that holds a printer. It uses a fabric vertical drawer sized for A4 or letter paper and rolls on casters.

It ranks fifth because it trades locking security for versatility. The printer shelf saves floor space, which the metal pedestals cannot do.

A good fit for small rooms that need a printer spot. The caveat is that a heavy printer limits how easily it rolls.
products.idealFor: Small rooms needing a printer spot.

products.name: BYNSOE 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Vertical Filing Storage Cabinet, Steel, Assembly Required
products.verdict: A standard steel cabinet that you must measure for.
products.description:
Steel body, vertical layout, two locking drawers: that is the whole BYNSOE pitch. Letter size paper only, and you build it yourself.

It ranks last because it has a standard file cabinet footprint rather than a narrow under-desk profile, and it takes only letter files. In the $50-100 bucket it offers less than the Letaya.

It works if you have generous space and want steel. The caveat is that you should measure your clearance before ordering.
products.skipIf: You need a narrow under-desk fit.

whatMatters.detail: Measure from floor to the underside of the desk and the depth to the modesty panel. A cabinet that is a few inches too tall will not slide in. Compare those numbers with the listing dimensions before ordering.
More drawers mean more capacity but also more height. Two drawers suit most home offices, while three suit an archive. Count your folders first and pick the smallest option that holds them.
A lock keeps financial and personal records secure. It matters in shared rooms or dorms. Check the title for the word lock and confirm whether keys are included.
Steel handles the weight of full hanging folders, while fabric drawers sag over time. Fabric is lighter and cheaper. Read the material line in the specs before judging.
Letter is the default in the US, but legal files are wider. If you handle legal documents, you need a drawer that fits them. Look for legal or A4 in the listing.

faq.q: Will a cabinet fit under every desk?
faq.a: No. Measure clearance height and depth first and compare them with the listing dimensions.

faq.q: Can I store legal size files?
faq.a: Only if the listing says so. The Letaya and SISESOL list legal support, while the BYNSOE lists letter only.

faq.q: Is a fabric cabinet good enough?
faq.a: For light paper it is. For heavy hanging folders, a steel cabinet is more stable.
The Letaya arrives assembled. Others need assembly, so plan time for it and keep the tools handy.

faq.q: Do the locks keep thieves out?
faq.a: They are meant for casual privacy, not security. Store sensitive originals in a proper safe.

faq.q: Can I move a rolling cabinet with a full load?
faq.a: Casters help, but a full cabinet is heavy. Lock the wheels when parked, and avoid overloading.

finalTake: The Letaya 3 drawer is the one we would buy, because it arrives built, locks and holds the most. If you are watching spending, the SISESOL gives you a narrow metal cabinet with a lock for less. Choose the GYIIYUO or DEVAISE only when mobility or surface space matters more than security.
